title: Range-edge persistence of cold-water Kelp forests at the southern European fringe
content:
Abstract
European environmental policies require reliable and up-to-date information to implement effective management and decision-making. Kelp forests are biodiversity-rich habitats that deliver key ecosystem services to human communities. In this context, the present study mapped subtidal macroalgal forests in Northern Portugal, a critical climatic biogeographical transitional zone for species range boundaries. By Dropcam technology, a total of 436 sites were sampled across a bathymetric range of 2–35 m depth. We classified the seabed according to the predominant substrate (sand, rock, or mixed sand-rock) while, in parallel, the eventual occurrences of macroalgae were registered. Although rocky and mixed sand-rock substrates accounted for 68.35% of the sampling sites, the occurrence of macroalgae was 38.07%. The most frequent case was the exclusive presence of Saccorhiza polyschides (20.64%), followed by sites solely dominated by Laminaria hyperborea (10.55%). In turn, L. ochroleuca was not observed. L. hyperborea and S. polyschides exhibited distinct depth-related distribution patterns. Both species reached their highest relative frequencies of occurrence at 4–8 m depth, but only L. hyperborea was notably present between 15 and 21 m. According to the SACFOR method, L. hyperborea was most frequently classified as Occasional, whereas S. polyschides was more often categorized as Abundant. In addition, the identification of four hotspots of L. hyperborea within the study area is particularly noteworthy, with Praia de Miramar (41.07°N) representing its southernmost recorded occurrence. Based on both official data and our observations, the total surface area collectively occupied by L. hyperborea and S. polyschides in Northern Portugal was estimated at 4950.43 ha. Although our results confirm this region as a climatically suitable area for cold-water species, main challenges associated with the persistence of L. hyperborea are discussed.
